question: Which Mauryan architectural structure is famous for its beautiful, sculpted gateways?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sanchi Stupa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Sanchi Stupa**, located in Madhya Pradesh, is one of the most renowned Buddhist monuments in India. It is famous for its beautifully sculpted gateways, known as **Toranas**.

• The gateways of the Sanchi Stupa are intricately carved and depict various **Buddhist symbols**, stories from Buddha's life, and Jataka tales that represent the moral and ethical teachings of Buddhism.

• The structure was commissioned by **Emperor Ashoka** in the 3rd century BCE during the Mauryan Empire and is considered one of the oldest stone structures in India.

• The central dome of the Sanchi Stupa symbolizes the **enlightenment** of the Buddha, while the gateways serve as a representation of the **four cardinal directions** and provide access to the circular pathway around the stupa.

• The Sanchi Stupa has been recognized as a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** since 1989 for its historical, cultural, and architectural significance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Features of Sanchi Stupa:**

• The stupa is a hemispherical dome with a central chamber that houses relics of the Buddha or other revered figures in Buddhism.

• The **Toranas** (gateways) are located in the four cardinal directions and are adorned with exquisite carvings depicting various events from the life of Buddha and his teachings.

• The circular path around the stupa, known as **Pradakshina Patha**, is meant for circumambulation, a sacred ritual in Buddhist practice.

• **Historical Background:**

• The Sanchi Stupa was commissioned by Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE and later expanded by the Shunga dynasty.

• It is a prominent example of Buddhist architecture and art during the Mauryan period.

• The stupas were used to house relics of the Buddha and serve as a place of meditation and devotion.

• **Other Options Explained:**

• **Amaravati Temple:** Located in Andhra Pradesh, this site is famous for its Buddhist stupas and sculptures but does not feature sculpted gateways like Sanchi Stupa.

• **Ajanta Caves:** Known for their rock-cut Buddhist caves and paintings, these caves are not associated with sculpted gateways.

• **Nalanda University:** An ancient center of learning in Bihar, it is renowned for its educational and architectural significance but does not have sculpted gateways like Sanchi Stupa.

• **Significance of Sanchi Stupa:**

• The stupa represents the **spread of Buddhism** in India during the Mauryan Empire.

• It serves as an important symbol of peace and enlightenment and is a major pilgrimage site for Buddhists worldwide.

• The intricate carvings on the gateways provide insights into the **artistic and cultural achievements** of the Mauryan and post-Mauryan periods.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Restoration Efforts:** The Sanchi Stupa underwent restoration during the colonial period by British officers like Sir John Marshall, ensuring its preservation for future generations.

• **Symbolism of the Stupa:** The dome symbolizes the **cosmic mountain**, and its umbrella-like structure represents the **three jewels of Buddhism** (Buddha, Dharma, Sangha).

• **Inscriptions:** The Sanchi Stupa features inscriptions in the **Brahmi script**, which provide valuable historical insights.

• **Influence on Later Architecture:** The architectural style of the Sanchi Stupa influenced the design of other stupas and Buddhist monuments across Asia.
